title: How Do Animals Do That? Fish, Birds and Bees
intro: Hi, friends! I'm Gizmo the robot, and welcome to Gizmo Explains!
I love asking, how does that work? Today we're going to find out how animals do amazing things.
We'll explore five cool things. Can you count them with me? One, two, three, four, five!
When my antenna lights up, it means I have an idea!

lines: Here's a clue: it swims, and it has fins and a tail! Can you guess?
How does it work? Let's find out!
Fish need air too, but they get it from water.
Water goes in their mouth and over their gills, and the gills take out the air they need!
Can you make a fish face and open and close your mouth?
What do fish use to breathe?
One more time, nice and loud: FISH!
That's why fish can stay underwater all day long.
Now we know how it works. Great job!
Here's a clue: it has feathers and wings, tweet tweet! Can you guess?
How does it work? Let's find out!
Birds flap their wings down to push on the air.
Pushing the air down and back lifts them up and moves them forward!
Can you flap your arms like wings? Flap, flap, flap!
How do birds stay light enough to fly?
Many birds have hollow bones and light feathers!
One more time, nice and loud: BIRD!
Their feathers are shaped just right for catching air.
Now we know how it works. Great job!
Here's a clue: it's fuzzy, it buzzes, and it loves flowers! Can you guess?
How does it work? Let's find out!
Honeybees drink a sweet juice from flowers, called nectar.
Back at the hive, they put it in little wax rooms and fan it with their wings until it turns into honey!
Can you buzz and fan your wings like a busy bee? Bzzz!
What do bees make honey from?
One more time, nice and loud: HONEYBEE!
The little wax rooms have six sides. They're called a honeycomb.
Now we know how it works. Great job!
Here's a clue: it has big, colorful wings! Can you guess?
How does it work? Let's find out!
A butterfly starts as a tiny egg, and then a hungry caterpillar hatches out.
The caterpillar makes a cozy case called a chrysalis. Inside, it changes into a butterfly!
Can you curl up small like a caterpillar, then open your wings wide?
What does a caterpillar turn into?
One more time, nice and loud: BUTTERFLY!
Egg, caterpillar, chrysalis, butterfly. What a change!
Now we know how it works. Great job!
Here's a clue: it swims on ponds and says quack, quack! Can you guess?
How does it work? Let's find out!
Ducks have a special oil near their tail.
They spread the oil on their feathers with their beak, so water rolls right off, and they stay dry!
Can you waddle like a duck? Quack, quack!
Why do ducks stay dry in the water?
Their oily feathers keep the water out!
One more time, nice and loud: DUCK!
Under their top feathers, ducks have soft fluffy feathers that keep them warm.
Now we know how it works. Great job!

recap: Wow, we learned so much! Let's remember.
Birds flap to push the air.
And ducks stay dry with oily feathers!
outro: Which one was your favorite? Keep asking, how does that work?
Bye, friends! See you next time on Gizmo Explains!
